title: Remove a bit from an unpowered handheld keyless drill
instruction: Remove the drill bit from the unpowered drill and leave the bit in the tray.
context: Carpenters routinely change drill bits while drilling and fastening; this task tests releasing a tool from radial chuck jaws while counterholding the loose drill.
setup: Three objects on the station counter: a 0.87 kg unpowered battery-removed polymer-housed drill with a steel chuck based on the DCD701 external 185 x 152 x 60 mm envelope lying on its side at x 320 / y 70 mm; a 6 x 93 mm steel round-shank bit (20.64 g) initially retained by three chuck jaws; and a 180 x 120 x 20 mm PP parts tray (100 g) centred at x 320 / y -65 mm. Sleeve diameter 42 mm and internal jaw geometry/forces are estimates. No fixture holds the drill or tray.
scoring: Score at the end. Every positive tier requires the intact bit entirely beyond the chuck nose by 20 mm, the drill supported on the counter with its lowest point within 3 mm of it, the bit supported at counter/tray height with its lowest point between 1 mm below and 25 mm above the counter, both hands released with all four actual pad tips and both midpoints 80 mm clear of every object collider, and under 1 mm motion over 21 samples at 20 Hz for the drill, sleeve, jaws, bit and tray. 0.5: these conditions. 1.0: also the complete bit inside the tray with 5 mm side margins, its lowest surface within 3 mm of the tray floor and its highest surface at most 19 mm above the tray base, with tray tilt at most 5 degrees and its lowest point within 3 mm of the counter. Gentle contact/repositioning is allowed. No opening angle or hidden release flag earns credit.
reset_notes: Restore the bit between the closed jaw faces and put the drill and tray in the stated starting poses.
fidelity: Rigid estimated DCD701 shell, 0.87 kg bare tool. Three inclined jaw slides use passive two-way nut/sleeve constraints: estimated 20 deg guides, 2 mm/rev lead, 0.15 Nm friction and 20 um initial interference. Native jaw-bit contact retains a loose 6 mm steel bit; the sleeve is hollow. Tool/tray contact, dimensions and mass splits are estimates. No spindle motor, bit flutes or material damage. Demo uses fixed waypoints.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 0.0 (bit removed into tray; signed nose-plane scoring condition fails)
